newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian president's popularity slides further.
newsitem.headline: Colombian president's popularity slides further.

text.p: Scandal-plagued President Ernesto Samper saw his popularity fall further in an opinion poll published by Colombia's leading daily on Sunday, in which 58 percent of those surveyed said he should resign.
While Samper's slide from grace, sparked by drug corruption allegations, has been gradual, his recently resigned vice-president Humberto de la Calle has fared even worse.
De la Calle formally quit his post last week, reigniting Colombia's political crisis and signalling his intention to become a major thorn in Samper's side.
His popularity has dropped from 42 percent four months ago to 31 percent, according to the telephone poll of 500 people published on Sunday in El Tiempo newspaper.
The survey shows that 41 percent of those questioned still back the embattled president, with greatest support from the over-40s and middle to low social classes.

"Opinions about Samper show a slow and progressive trend. His positive image is decreasing while his negative image is growing. But there is nothing to suggest that in a few months time he will no longer have any grassroots support, " El Tiempo said.
When De la Calle quit his post he said the president's alleged ties to drugs barons had undermined the government's credibility and were tearing the country apart.
He insisted Samper knew that the Cali Cartel had pumped millions of dollars of drugs cash into the 1994 campaign that brought him to power. Samper has denied these charges.
Samper named veteran politician and Colombia's ambassador to Britain, Carlos Lemos Simmonds, to replace De la Calle. Congress is expected to ratify the nomination on Thursday.
